{{Elections in Michigan}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in Michigan''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Michigan]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former Wayne County health director [[Abdul El-Sayed]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former congressman [[Mike Rogers (Michigan politician)|Mike Rogers]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Democratic incumbent [[Gary Peters]] is not seeking a third term.

For most of the primary, El-Sayed, congresswoman [[Haley Stevens]], and state senator [[Mallory McMorrow]] sought the Democratic nomination. After McMorrow withdrew in July, El-Sayed and Stevens remained in a tight race, which El-Sayed won on August 4 with 48.5% of the vote. Rogers, the Republican nominee in [[2024 United States Senate election in Michigan|2024]], was the only candidate to qualify for his party's primary ballot.

This is the only open Democratic-held Senate seat up for election in a state won by [[Donald Trump]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. Republicans have not won a Senate race in Michigan since [[1994 United States Senate election in Michigan|1994]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 6, 2025 |title=These are the candidates running for Michigan's open Senate seat in 2026 |url=https://michiganindependent.com/politics/candidates-running-for-michigans-open-senate-seat-in-2026/ |access-date=August 4, 2025 |website=The Michigan Independent |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Background ==
Michigan is regarded as a [[battleground state|swing state]]. Most recently in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Michigan|2020]] and [[2024 United States presidential election in Michigan|2024]] presidential elections, it backed [[Joe Biden]] by 2.8% and [[Donald Trump]] by 1.4%, respectively.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 5, 2024 |title=Michigan Presidential Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-michigan-president.html |access-date=January 29, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Gary Peters was first elected with 54.6% of the vote in [[2014 United States Senate election in Michigan|2014]] and re-elected with 49.9% in [[2020 United States Senate election in Michigan|2020]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mielections.us/election/results/14GEN/|title = 2014 Michigan Official General Election Results - 11/04/2014 |website=Michigan Secretary of State |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240716012120/https://mielections.us/election/results/14GEN/ |archive-date=July 16, 2024|access-date=July 22, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=November 3, 2020 |title=Michigan U.S. Senate Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2020/11/03/us/elections/results-michigan-senate.html |access-date=July 22, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> He announced in January 2025 he was not seeking reelection for a third term.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howard |first=Andrew |date=January 28, 2025 |title=Gary Peters not running for reelection in battleground Michigan |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/01/28/gary-peters-not-running-for-reelection-in-battleground-michigan-00200925 |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=Politico}}</ref>

Both parties have had electoral success in Michigan in recent years, though Democrats have performed better in non-presidential races. Democrats currently hold both [[List of United States senators from Michigan|U.S. Senate seats]], all statewide executive offices, and the [[Michigan Senate|state senate]]. Republicans control the [[Michigan House of Representatives]] and hold a majority of the state's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] seats.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 6, 2024 |title=Democrats lose trifecta in Michigan, hobbling Gov. Whitmer's agenda |url=https://apnews.com/article/michigan-house-races-democrats-trifecta-35669bb7d15261abf4219e6f57df7769 |access-date=January 29, 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan since [[1994 United States Senate election in Michigan|1994]], this Senate seat since [[1972 United States Senate election in Michigan|1972]] or a non-presidential statewide election since [[2014 United States elections|2014]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Spangler |first1=Todd |date=January 28, 2025 |title=Michigan's Gary Peters won't run for US Senate reelection next year |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/2025/01/28/gary-peters-us-senate-2026/77993125007/ |access-date=January 28, 2025 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]]}}</ref>

As one of two Democratic-held Senate seats in a state won by Donald Trump in 2024, Michigan is considered a key Senate battleground in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gans |first=Jared |date=November 28, 2024 |title=7 most competitive Senate races in 2026 |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5013277-2026-key-senate-races-watch/ |access-date=January 28, 2025 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="NBC Retire"/>

== Democratic primary ==
=== Campaign ===
[[Mallory McMorrow]], who was first elected to the [[Michigan Senate]] in 2018, announced her campaign for the U.S. Senate on April 2, 2025, becoming the first high-profile Democrat to enter the race to succeed Gary Peters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Volmert |first=Isabella |date=April 2, 2025|title=Michigan lawmaker Mallory McMorrow announces Democratic bid for US Senate |url=https://apnews.com/article/mallory-mcmorrow-2026-election-michigan-senate-1e5f694a199cac0b48c37cb0bd99298d |access-date=July 21, 2026|website=[[Associated Press]] }}</ref> Her campaign launch featured footage from a 2022 speech defending her support for transgender individuals following criticism from Republican colleagues.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wu |first=Nicholas |date=April 3, 2025 |title=Mallory McMorrow announces bid for U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Peters |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/mallory-mcmorrow-announces-bid-for-u-s-senate/ |access-date=July 22, 2026|website=[[CBS News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wu |first=Nicholas |date=April 2, 2025 |title=State Sen. Mallory McMorrow announces Michigan Senate bid |url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2025/04/02/congress/mcmorrow-launches-senate-bid-00264967 |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=[[Politico]]}}</ref> [[Abdul El-Sayed]], former director of [[Wayne County, Michigan|Wayne County]]'s Department of Health, Human and Veteran Services, entered the race on April 19, 2025.<ref name="El-Sayed Launch">{{Cite web |last=Wu |first=Nicholas |title=Abdul El-Sayed launches Michigan Senate campaign |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/17/abdul-el-sayed-michigan-senate-campaign-00293627 |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=[[Politico]]}}</ref> [[Haley Stevens]], who has represented [[Michigan's 11th congressional district|Michigan's 11th congressional]] district since 2019, announced her candidacy three days later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=King |first=Jon |date=April 22, 2025 |title=Haley Stevens announces run for US Senate, becoming the 3rd Democrat seeking to replace Gary Peters |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2025/04/22/haley-stevens-announces-run-for-us-senate-becoming-the-3rd-democrat-seeking-to-replace-gary-peters/ |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=[[Michigan Advance]]}}</ref> By March 2026, McMorrow had collected more than 30,000 volunteer-gathered signatures, qualifying for the ballot without paid petition circulators.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solis |first=Ben |date=March 23, 2026 |title=McMorrow touts volunteer push to reach 30K petition signatures in U.S. Senate race |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2026/03/23/mcmorrow-touts-volunteer-push-to-reach-30k-petition-signatures-in-u-s-senate-race/ |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=[[Michigan Advance]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In April 2026, Stevens and El-Sayed also qualified for the ballot after collecting the required signatures.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2026 |title=Haley Stevens Takes Questions As She Submits Petition Signatures For U.S. Senate Run |url=https://home.mirs.news/post/haley-stevens-takes-questions-as-she-submits-petition-signatures-for-u-s-senate-run |access-date=July three candidates spoke at the Michigan Democratic Party's Spring Endorsement Convention in [[Detroit]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hermani |first=Jordyn |date=April 20, 2026 |title=Michigan Democrats push party left. Will voters follow? |url=https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/michigan-democrats-push-party-left-will-voters-follow/ |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=[[Bridge Michigan]]}}</ref>

Stevens, McMorrow, and El-Sayed each represented different ideological wings and campaign strategies within the Democratic Party. Stevens, who received private backing from Senate Democratic leadership, was viewed as the more [[Political moderate|moderate]] candidate, while El-Sayed was considered the most [[Progressivism|progressive]].<ref name="Identity Crisis">{{Cite web |last=Vincent |first=Robyn |date=March 18, 2026 |title=Michigan Senate primary: A Democratic identity crisis race|url=https://michiganadvance.com/2025/11/24/field-shaping-up-in-michigans-contested-u-s-senate-race/ |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=[[Michigan Advance]] |language=en-US}}</ref> El-Sayed |language=en-US |issn=0040-781X}}</ref> McMorrow centered her campaign on the need for new Democratic leadership and pledged not to support [[Chuck Schumer]] as Senate Democratic [[party leaders of — Without Chuck Schumer |url=https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2025/03/25/mallory-mcmorrow-michigan-senate-chuck-schumer-00246369 |access-date=July 22, 2026|website=[[Politico]]|last=Wren|first=Adam}}</ref> El-Sayed criticized that position, arguing it was shortsighted to oppose Schumer without identifying a successor.<ref name="El-Sayed Launch"/> Stevens emphasized her role in helping rescue the [[Big Three (automobile manufacturers)|Big Three]] automakers during the Obama administration, while McMorrow and El-Sayed promoted diversifying Michigan's economy through apprenticeships in industries such as [[beekeeping]], [[winemaking]], and leather-making.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gomez |first=Henry J. |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Hive mind: McMorrow withdrew from the race in July 2026 after her polling declined.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Michigan Democrat Mallory McMorrow drops out of Senate race, leaving Stevens-El-Sayed showdown |url=https://planetdetroit.org/2026/07/mcmorrow-exits-michigan-senate-race/ |access-date=July 15, 2026 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |via=Planet Detroit |language=en-CA}}</ref><ref In the days leading up to the election, polls had showed El-Sayed with a double digit lead.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hernandez |first1=Alec |last2=Doherty |first2=Erin |last3=Pellish |first3=Aaron |language=en|last=Gnewikow|first=Tara}}</ref>

Campaign finance emerged as a point of contrast during the primary. El-Sayed and McMorrow called for an end to corporate political spending and declined corporate donations during the election cycle, while Stevens expressed support for campaign finance reform and said she was "not taking any new pledges."<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Mauger |first=Craig |title=Progressive uprising divides Democrats up and down Michigan's ballot |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2026/07/16/michigan-progressive-democrats-abdul-el-sayed-donavan-mckinney-will-lawrence-chris-gilmer-hill/90914455007/ |access-date=July 16, 2026 |website=[[The Detroit News]] |language=en-US|date=July 16, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Shunned Corporate PAC Money">{{Cite web |last=Nann Burke |first=Melissa |date=August 14, 2025 |title=Two Michigan Senate hopefuls have shunned corporate PAC money. One is raking it in |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/14/michigan-senate-corporate-pac-donations-haley-stevens-abdul-el-sayed-mallory-mcmorrow-mike-rogers/85640264007/ |access-date=July 25, 2026 |website=[[The Detroit News]]}}</ref> Financial disclosure also became an issue after Stevens urged El-Sayed to release his financial disclosure report before the August 4 primary. El-Sayed had previously received an extension to file the report until August 13 but released his 2026 financial returns publicly in July.<ref name="Kelly House">{{Cite web |last=House |first=Kelly |date=July 22, 2026 |title=Fact-check: Millionaire claims in Abdul El-Sayed, Haley Stevens Senate race |url=https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/fact-check-millionaire-claims-in-abdul-el-sayed-haley-stevens-senate-race/ |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=[[Bridge Michigan]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Laplante">{{Cite web |last=Laplante |first=Brad |date=July 15, 2026 |title=El-Sayed releases tax return ahead of primary |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5970084-michigan-el-sayed-tax-returns/ |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}</ref>

Policy differences between the candidates centered on [[Immigration policy of the United States|immigration]], foreign policy, and healthcare.<ref name="MichiganAdvancePolicy" /> Israel emerged as a major issue in the race. El-Sayed, who is considered more [[pro-Palestinian]] and the most critical of Israel of all the candidates, called for ending all unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel. In contrast, Stevens has voted to provide additional military aid to Israel, has received significant support from the [[pro-Israel]] [[lobbying group]] [[AIPAC]], and stated she does not believe there has been a genocide in Gaza.<ref name="auto2"/> She supports a [[two-state solution]]<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Bradner |first1=Eric |last2=Wright |first2=David |date=July 8, 2026 |title=El-Sayed and Stevens clash over AIPAC and other takeaways from the Michigan Senate debate|url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/07/politics/michigan-senate-debate-abdul-el-sayed-haley-stevens |access-date=July 16, 2026 |work=[[CNN]] |language=en}}</ref> and criticized [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]], accusing him of endangering Jewish people worldwide.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Haley Stevens grabs Benjamin Netanyahu's lifeline on Israel |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/07/haley-stevens-gets-a-lifeline-on-israel-00989605|last1=Kashinsky|first1=Lisa|last2=Benson|first2=Samuel|access-date=July 15, 2026 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en|date=July 7, 2026}}</ref><ref name="MichiganAdvancePolicy">{{Cite web |last=Alexandrakis |first=George |date=June 9, 2026 |title=Michigan's U.S. Senate primary highlights divisions within Democratic Party |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2026/06/09/stevens-mcmorrow-el-sayed-clash-over-foreign-policy-party-leadership-as-primary-approaches/ |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=[[Michigan Advance]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gibbons |first=Lauren |date=July 13, 2026 |title=Outside spending floods Michigan's US Senate race — most for Haley Stevens |url=https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/outside-spending-floods-michigans-us-senate-race-most-for-haley-stevens/ |access-date=July 16, 2026 |website=[[Bridge Michigan]] |language=en-US}}</ref> On domestic policy, El-Sayed supports [[Medicare for All]] and the abolition of [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]], while Stevens has called for the expansion of Medicare access and reforming ICE.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Niko |date=July 25, 2026 |title=Governor Gretchen Whitmer endorses Rep. Haley Stevens for Senate |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/news-briefs/governor-gretchen-whitmer-endorses-rep-haley-stevens-for-senate/ |access-date=July 25, 2026 |website=[[The Michigan Daily]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wren |first=Adam |date=February 1, 2026 |title=Michigan's 3-car pileup of a primary has Senate Democrats worried |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/01/michigan-senate-mcmorrow-stevens-el-sayed-00758408 |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref> El-Sayed has faced criticism for claiming that he never supported the [[Defund the police|Defund the Police]] movement, despite previously promoting it on [[Detroit public radio|Detroit Public Radio]] and social media.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Kaczynski|first1=Andrew|last2=Steck|first2=Em |date=July 7, 2026 |title='We do need to defund the police': 2020 interviews undermine Abdul El-Sayed's claim he never advocated for unpopular movement |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/07/politics/kfile-abdul-el-sayed-michigan-senate-defund-police-fact-check |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[CNN]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Nann Burke |first1=Melissa |last2=Mauger |first2=Craig |last3=LeBlanc |first3=Beth |date=November 15, 2025 |title=Insider: Abdul El-Sayed distances himself from past defund-the-police rhetoric |url=https://eu.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2025/11/15/abdul-el-sayed-distances-himself-from-past-defund-the-police-rhetoric/87276996007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116082605/https://eu.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2025/11/15/abdul-el-sayed-distances-himself-from-past-defund-the-police-rhetoric/87276996007/ |archive-date=November 16, 2025 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[The Detroit News]]}}</ref>

''The Associated Press'' called the race for El-Sayed the morning after the election who had roughly a one percent lead over Stevens with 99% of the votes reporting. That same day, Stevens called El-Sayed to concede the race and pledged to support him in the general election against Mike Rogers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gibbons |first=Lauren |date=August 5, 2026 |title=Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary in progressive 'shockwave' |url=https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/michigan-democratic-senate-primary-results-abdul-el-sayed-haley-stevens/ |access-date=August 6, 2026 |website=[[Bridge Michigan]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cappelletti |first=Joey |date=August 5, 2026 |title=How Abdul El-Sayed went from political oblivion to progressive breakthrough in Michigan Senate race |url=https://apnews.com/article/michigan-primary-senate-elsayed-stevens-60c79349b60ffbf24a34d60b76e130ed |access-date=August 6, 2026 |website=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Following Stevens' defeat, an AIPAC spokesperson stated: "Our members remain determined to ensure that voters reject Dr. El-Sayed and his radical anti-Israel agenda in November."<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIPAC, Soros and the Money That Has Shaped Michigan's Senate Race |url=https://www.newsweek.com/aipac-soros-money-shaping-michigans-senate-race-12532088 |access-date=October 10, 2026 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref>

===Analysis===
Stevens benefited from an outside spending advantage, with approximately $62 million spent on her behalf, amounting to a 9–1 advantage to El-Sayed.<ref name="AIPAC91">{{Cite news |last=Schleifer |first=Theodore |date=August 4, 2026 |title=Spending Tied to AIPAC Dominated the Michigan Senate Primary |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/04/us/politics/michigan-democratic-senate-primary-aipac.html |access-date=August 14, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> [[AIPAC]] and affiliated pro-Israel political groups spent nearly $30 million supporting Stevens, surpassing all of their prior investments made for a candidate in a particular race.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2026 |title=AIPAC spends nearly $30M on Stevens over Al-Sayed in Michigan Senate primary, its largest single-race investment ever |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/aipac-michigan-senate-primary-stevens-abdul-el-sayed/ |access-date=July 27, 2026 |website=[[CBS News]] }}</ref> Their primary political action committee, The United Democracy Project, released a Michigan advertisement featuring a 2018 clip of [[Barack Obama]] praising Stevens for her work as chief of staff to a federal task force created to assist the automobile industry in 2009.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news |last=Epstein |first=Reid J. |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Can a Pro-Israel Democrat Still Win a Big Primary? She's Going to Try. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/16/us/politics/haley-stevens-michigan-senate-israel-aipac.html |access-date=July 19, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name="cnnjuly17">{{Cite news |last=Wright |first=David |date=July 17, 2026 |title=Barack Obama hasn't endorsed a Michigan Senate candidate. An AIPAC-linked group is spending millions on ads with him anyway |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/17/politics/obama-michigan-senate-stevens-el-sayed-ads |access-date=July 19, 2026 |work=[[CNN]] |language=en}}</ref>

El-Sayed harnessed Democratic frustration with the party establishment to narrowly defeat Stevens in the primary.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cappelletti |first=Joey |date=August 5, 2026 |title=How Abdul El-Sayed went from political oblivion to progressive breakthrough in Michigan Senate race |url=https://apnews.com/article/60c79349b60ffbf24a34d60b76e130ed |access-date=September 6, 2026 |work=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> ''The Washington Post'' said that several factors helped with El-Sayed's success, including antiestablishment sentiment in the Democratic base, his campaign against large political donations, and opposition to AIPAC and Israel's actions in Gaza.<ref name="WaPoPrimaryAnalysis">{{Cite news |last1=Goodwin |first1=Liz |last2=Cox |first2=Erin |last3=Morse |first3=Clara Ence |last4=Marley |first4=Patrick |date=August 5, 2026 |title=How El-Sayed won the contentious Michigan Senate Democratic primary |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/08/05/how-el-sayed-won-contentious-michigan-senate-democratic-primary/ |access-date=September 6, 2026 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref> El-Sayed performed well in liberal strongholds and college towns in his win over Stevens.<ref name="PrimaryTurnout">{{Cite web |last=Mencarini |first=Matt |date=August 5, 2026 |title=How Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan: Big turnout, liberal towns, walkup votes |url=https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/how-abdul-el-sayed-won-michigan-big-turnout-liberal-towns-walkup-votes/ |access-date=September 6, 2026 |website=[[Bridge Michigan]]}}</ref>

[[Bernie Sanders|Senator Bernie Sanders]] also said in a tweet that [[AIPAC]] planned to spend $233 million to defeat candidates who oppose Benjamin Netanyahu's government. He also said: "They spent $33 million to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan primary, but they lost."<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2026 |title=US senator says AIPAC plans to spend $233M to defeat candidates critical of Netanyahu gov't |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-senator-says-aipac-plans-to-spend-233m-to-defeat-candidates-critical-of-netanyahu-govt/4076743 |access-date=October 12, 2026 |website=Anadolu |language=tr}}</ref>

In the primary election, El-Sayed won the election by carrying 30 of the state's 83 counties, including nine in the [[Upper Peninsula of Michigan|Upper Peninsula]] and an additional nine north of [[Grand Rapids, Michigan|Grand Rapids]]. Stevens performed well in [[Metro Detroit]], [[The Thumb]], and much of [[Northern Michigan]].<ref name="PrimaryTurnout" /> She carried the majority of the vote in Michigan's suburban areas by five percentage points, whereas El-Sayed had his strongest showing with voters aged 18–34 and those living in cities outside of Detroit.<ref name="WaPoPrimaryAnalysis" />

==Republican primary==
===Campaign===
Michigan was considered one of the top Republican senate pickup opportunities for the 2026 cycle, and national Republicans quickly coalesced around their [[2024 United States Senate election in Michigan|2024]] senate nominee, former congressman [[Mike Rogers (Michigan politician)|Mike Rogers]], as their preferred candidate. Rogers' only significant opposition was from former co-chair of the [[Michigan Republican Party]] Bernadette Smith, who had vacated this position one week prior to the launch of her candidacy. [[Fox News]] labeled her campaign as a "longshot" due to [[Donald Trump]] having already endorsed Rogers prior to Smith's entrance into the race, and because of her criminal record, which included a [[Nolo contendere|no-contest]] plea of felony [[welfare fraud]] and a guilty conviction for seriously injuring a ten-year-old boy in an automobile accident.<ref name="Clash">{{cite web|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/michigan-gop-leader-signals-senate-bid-sets-up-clash-trump-endorsed-mike-rogers |title=Former Michigan GOP leader signals Senate bid, sets up clash with Trump-endorsed Mike Rogers |website=[[Fox News]] |last1=Steinhauser |first1=Paul |date=November 12, 2025 |access-date=August 10, 2026}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=August 2026}} Smith did not make the primary ballot after being disqualified by the Board of State Canvassers for not submitting the required number of signatures, thus allowing Rogers to win the nomination uncontested.<ref name=BSC/>
